Detailed Description

AVL tree.

This tree is a standard AVL tree implementation that stores elements in the order defined by the comparison function.

Duplicate elements are allowed. They are visited in insertion order. Use tommy_tree_insert_unique() to reject duplicate keys.

To initialize a tree you have to call tommy_tree_init() specifying a comparison function that will define the order in the tree.

tommy_tree tree;
tommy_tree_init(&tree, cmp);

Initializes the tree.
Definition: tommytree.h:157

To insert elements in the tree you have to call tommy_tree_insert() for each element. In the insertion call you have to specify the address of the node and the address of the element. The address of the element is used to initialize the tommy_node::data field of the node.

struct element {
int value;
// other fields
tommy_tree_node node;
};
struct element* elem = malloc(sizeof(struct element)); // creates the element
elem->value = ...; // initializes the element
tommy_tree_insert(&tree, &elem->node, elem); // inserts the element

Inserts an element in the tree, allowing duplicate keys.

To find the first element with a given key in tree order, call tommy_tree_search() providing the key to search.

struct element value_to_find = { 1 };
struct element* elem = tommy_tree_search(&tree, &value_to_find);
if (!elem) {
// not found
} else {
// found
}
tommy_tree_search

Searches an element in the tree.
Definition: tommytree.h:447

To iterate over all the elements in the tree you can call tommy_tree_head() to get the head of the tree and follow the next elements with tommy_tree_next().

tommy_tree_node* i = tommy_tree_head(&tree);
while (i) {
struct element* elem = i->data; // gets the element pointer
printf("%d\n", elem->value); // process the element
i = tommy_tree_next(i); // go to the next element
}

Definition: tommytree.h:257

Iterators are pointers to nodes contained in the tree. Inserting elements or removing other nodes between iterator calls does not invalidate pointers to nodes that remain in the tree. Subsequent next/prev calls use the current contents and ordering; inserted elements may become visible and removed elements are skipped.

Removing the pointed node invalidates its use as an iterator, even if its storage has not been freed. To continue traversal after removing the current node, obtain the next or previous node before removal.

Keys and fields used for ordering must not be modified while contained. Concurrent traversal and modification require external synchronization.

To remove the first element with a given key in tree order, call tommy_tree_remove() providing the key to search and remove.

struct element value_to_remove = { 1 };
struct element* elem = tommy_tree_remove(&tree, &value_to_remove);
if (elem) {
free(elem); // frees the element allocated memory
}
tommy_tree_remove
void * tommy_tree_remove(tommy_tree *tree, const void *data)
Searches and removes an element from the tree.
Definition: tommytree.h:789

You can also remove an element from the tree if you already have the node address using tommy_tree_remove_existing().

struct element* elem = ...;
tommy_tree_remove_existing(&tree, &elem->node);
free(elem);
tommy_tree_remove_existing
TOMMY_API void * tommy_tree_remove_existing(tommy_tree *tree, tommy_tree_node *node)
Removes an element from the tree.

To remove the smallest or greatest element you can use tommy_tree_remove_head() or tommy_tree_remove_tail().

struct element* elem = tommy_tree_remove_head(&tree);
if (elem) {
free(elem);
}
tommy_tree_remove_head
void * tommy_tree_remove_head(tommy_tree *tree)
Removes and returns the head (smallest) element.
Definition: tommytree.h:344

To destroy the tree you have to remove or destroy all the contained elements. The tree itself doesn't have or need a deallocation function. This can be done with the tommy_tree_foreach() function.

// deallocates all the elements iterating the tree
tommy_tree_foreach(&tree, free);

typedef tommy_node tommy_tree_node

Tree node.

This is the node that you have to include inside your elements. The node must preserve its natural alignment because the tree stores the balance factor in the two least significant bits of the parent pointer.

◆ tommy_tree_swap()

void tommy_tree_swap ( tommy_tree *  first,
tommy_tree *  second 
)

Exchanges the contents of two initialized trees, including their comparison functions.

Each comparison function moves with its root to preserve the tree order. The trees must not share nodes. Nodes are not accessed or modified. Passing the same tree twice has no effect.

Parameters
firstThe first tree.
secondThe second tree.
Note
This operation is O(1).

◆ tommy_tree_clear()

void tommy_tree_clear ( tommy_tree *  tree)

Removes all elements, preserving the comparison function.

The tree remains initialized and can be reused immediately. Elements are not freed and nodes are not accessed or modified. Their links must not be used to traverse the previous contents. You can call this function after tommy_tree_foreach() has freed the elements.

Parameters
treeThe tree.
Note
This operation is O(1).

tommy_tree_node *  node,
void *  data 
)

Inserts an element only if no equal element is already contained.

If found, the first equal element in tree order is returned and the candidate node is left unchanged. Otherwise the candidate is inserted and data is returned.

Parameters
treeThe tree.
nodeThe candidate node. It must not belong to any container.
dataPointer to the element to insert.
Returns
The first equal element, or data if the candidate was inserted.

◆ tommy_tree_to_list()

TOMMY_API void tommy_tree_to_list ( tommy_tree *  tree,
tommy_list *  list 
)

Transfers all elements from the tree to the tail of a list in tree order.

Existing list elements remain before the transferred elements. The tree is left empty and initialized with its original comparison function. The list must be initialized and must not share nodes with the tree. Elements are not freed, and the node data and index fields are left unchanged. The index field no longer represents a valid tree parent after the transfer.

Parameters
treeThe tree to drain.
listThe destination list.
Note
This operation is O(n), using O(log n) stack space.

◆ tommy_tree_find_compare()

tommy_tree_node * tommy_tree_find_compare ( tommy_tree *  tree,
tommy_compare_func *  cmp,
const void *  cmp_arg 
)

Finds the first equal node in the tree with a specific comparison function.

Like tommy_tree_find() but you can specify a different comparison function. Note that this function must define a suborder of the original one. The first equal node in tree order is returned.

The cmp_arg argument will be the first argument of the comparison function, and it can be of a different type than the elements in the tree.

Parameters
treeThe tree.
cmpComparison function called with cmp_arg and the element in the tree.
cmp_argSearch key, which may have a different type from tree elements.
Returns
The first equal node in tree order, or 0 if none.

◆ tommy_tree_foreach()

TOMMY_API void tommy_tree_foreach ( tommy_tree *  tree,
tommy_foreach_func *  func 
)

Calls the specified function for each element in the tree.

The elements are processed in order.

You cannot add or remove elements from the inside of the callback, but can use it to deallocate them.

tommy_tree tree;
// initializes the tree
tommy_tree_init(&tree, cmp);
...
// creates an element
struct element* elem = malloc(sizeof(struct element));
...
// insert it in the tree
tommy_tree_insert(&tree, &elem->node, elem);
...
// deallocates all the elements iterating the tree
tommy_tree_foreach(&tree, free);
tommy_tree_clear(&tree); // resets the tree before reuse
tommy_tree_clear
void tommy_tree_clear(tommy_tree *tree)
Removes all elements, preserving the comparison function.
Definition: tommytree.h:189

If the callback frees the elements, the tree retains dangling node pointers. Call tommy_tree_clear() or tommy_tree_init() before reusing it. The tree has no storage to release.

Parameters
treeThe tree.
funcFunction to call with each element.

◆ tommy_tree_foreach_arg()

TOMMY_API void tommy_tree_foreach_arg ( tommy_tree *  tree,
tommy_foreach_arg_func *  func,
void *  arg 
)

Calls the specified function with an argument for each element in the tree.

The iteration order and callback rules are the same as tommy_tree_foreach(). The callback may deallocate the current element. Adding or removing elements from inside the callback is not allowed.

Parameters
treeThe tree.
funcFunction to call with each element.
argArgument to pass to the function.
